title: Variables, Expressions & Statements
short_description: Learn how to store data, write expressions, and use operators.
bro_quote: A variable is a named container that holds a value—the foundation of all programming logic.

subtopics.name: What is a Variable?
subtopics.explanation:
• 📦 A variable is a named storage container. When you write age = 20, you are telling Python: "Create a box, label it 'age', and put the number 20 inside it."
  • 🏷️ The name is on the left, the value is on the right. The = sign means "store this value".
  • 🔄 You can change a variable's value anytime. The old value is simply replaced.
  • 🧩 Variable names should be descriptive. Use age instead of just x.

subtopics.name: Naming Rules for Variables
subtopics.explanation:
• ✅ Names can contain letters, numbers, and underscores ( _ ).
  • 🚫 Names CANNOT start with a number.
  • 🚫 Names CANNOT have spaces. Use an underscore instead.
  • 🔡 Python is case-sensitive. age and Age are different.

subtopics.name: The print() Function
subtopics.explanation:
• 🖨️ print() shows output on the screen. It is how your program talks to you.
  • 📝 You can print text, variables, or numbers. Just put them inside the parentheses.
  • ➕ You can print multiple things at once. Separate them with commas.

subtopics.name: Understanding f-strings (Formatted Strings)
subtopics.explanation:
• ✨ The f in f"..." stands for "formatted." It tells Python to format the string with variables inside.
  • 🔤 Inside an f-string, use curly braces {} to insert variables. Example: f"Hello {name}"
  • 💡 Variables inside {} are replaced with their actual values. NOT printed as literal text.
  • ⚡ f-strings are cleaner and easier to read than other string joining methods.
  • 🎯 You can put expressions inside {}, not just variable names. Example: f"Sum: {5 + 3}"
  • 💾 f-strings must start with the letter f before the opening quote. Write f"...", not "..."

snippets.code:
name = "Bob"
age = 25
print(f"My name is {name} and I'm {age} years old.")

a = 10
b = 5
print(f"Sum: {a + b}")        # Sum: 15
print(f"Product: {a * b}")   # Product: 50

name = "Alice"
age = 25
# The old way (messier)
print("My name is " + name + " and I'm " + str(age) + " years old.")
# The f-string way (cleaner)
print(f"My name is {name} and I'm {age} years old.")

subtopics.name: Data Types — What Kind of Data Can You Store?
subtopics.explanation:
• 🔢 Integer (int) — Whole numbers. Like 5 or 100.
  • 🌊 Float — Decimal numbers. Like 3.14 or 9.99.
  • 📝 String (str) — Text wrapped in quotes. Like "Hello".
  • ✅ Boolean (bool) — True or False. Like a light switch.

snippets.code:
age = 20        # int
price = 9.99    # float
name = "Alice"  # str
is_on = True    # bool

subtopics.name: Basic Operators — Doing Math in Python
subtopics.explanation:
• ➕ Addition ( + ) and Subtraction ( - )
  • ✖️ Multiplication ( * ) and Division ( / )
  • 📐 Floor Division ( // ) — removes the decimal.
  • 🔁 Modulus ( % ) — gives the remainder.

snippets.code:
a = 10
b = 3
print(a + b)  # 13
print(a * b)  # 30

subtopics.name: Order of Operations
subtopics.explanation:
• 📚 Follows standard math rules. Parentheses first, then Multiply/Divide, then Add/Subtract.
  • 💡 When in doubt, use parentheses. They make your code clear.

subtopics.name: Working with Strings (Text)
subtopics.explanation:
• ➕ Join strings using +. This is called concatenation.
  • 🔗 f-strings make mixing text and variables easy. Use f"Text {variable}".

subtopics.name: Taking User Input
subtopics.explanation:
• ⌨️ input() lets your program ask the user for data. It pauses and waits for the user to type and press Enter.
  • 📝 The prompt text appears before the input field. Example: input("What's your name? ")
  • 🔤 input() always returns a string. Even if the user types a number, it's stored as text.
  • 🔢 Convert to other types using int(), float(), bool().
  • ⚠️ Be careful with type conversion. Converting "abc" to int will cause an error.

snippets.code:
name = input("What is your name? ")
print(f"Hello, {name}!")

age = int(input("How old are you? "))
print(f"Next year: {age + 1}")

price = float(input("Enter price: "))
print(f"Total with tax: ${price * 1.1:.2f}")

questions: 1. Use input() to ask the user for their name and then print a greeting. (Basic input)
2. Ask the user for their age as input and convert it to an integer. (Integer input)
3. Take a price as input from the user and convert it to a float. (Float input)
4. Ask the user for two numbers, add them together, and print the result. (Integer calculations)
5. Take three different inputs (name, age, height) and store them in variables. (Multiple inputs)
6. Ask the user for a number and calculate the remainder when divided by 3. (Modulus with input)
7. Take two prices from the user and calculate the total with tax (10%). (Float calculations)
8. Ask the user for their name and use f-string to display a formatted message. (F-strings with input)
9. Take an integer input and print its data type using type(). (Type checking input)
10. Take user input for a base and height, then calculate the area of a rectangle. (Practical problem)
